title: Piecemeal restore strategy and verification guide for private deploys
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures a pragmatic, piecemeal restore approach for private deployments (VPC / on-prem) when full-site restore is either unnecessary or too risky. Focus: bring a minimal critical path online quickly (API + control plane query surface) and iterate to full state. Designed for mid-sized private deploys (1–10 racks or equivalent cloud VPCs).

Why piecemeal?
- Full restores are time-consuming and riskier (schema drift, long WAL replay).
- Many customer incidents only require a subset of services to be functional (ingest, admin API, model reads) while background subsystems catch up.

High-level restore modes (choose one based on outage profile):
1) Critical-path restore (fast): restore control plane DB read-replicas, object storage with current model artifacts, minimal router/proxy, and inference pods in read-only mode.
2) Partial failover (balanced): restore datastore primaries, KV store, model serving, and limited write paths for customer traffic with strict throttling.
3) Full rehydrate (last resort): full snapshot replay, WAL application, and schema migration — used only when data loss is unacceptable.

Initial triage checklist (first 15–30 min)
- Confirm incident scope: region(s), on-prem racks, or VPC subnets impacted.
- Determine data durability guarantees broken (object storage, DB, Kafka).
- Check last successful snapshot timestamps for each backend (S3-compatible, Postgres, etc.).
- Identify where tfstate lives and whether it’s intact / locked.
- Slack/Zoom: @oncall, @infra, customer success lead added.

Piecemeal restore sequence (recommended order)
1) Communication & isolation
   - Create incident channel, collect contact points, and declare Tiers (P0/P1).
   - If on-prem network partially healthy, enable management VLAN access for operators only.

2) Protect current state
   - Snapshot any remaining volumes and object store buckets (read-only export).
   - Create offsite transfer if local storage compromised.

3) Terraform considerations (notes and gotchas)
   - Avoid full-apply where possible. Use targeted applies: terraform apply -target=module.network -target=module.kubernetes.
   - Lock state before any changes (remote state backend MUST be accessible). If state is lost, follow import flow (see below).
   - Confirm terraform provider versions. Upgrades to TF >1.5 have known provider ordering changes; prefer the same version used in last successful run.
   - When bringing up K8s clusters, avoid automatic nodepool autoscaling until control plane is verified.
   - Import step example: terraform import module.db.aws_db_instance.primary <instance-id> — record import mappings in incident notes.
   - For modules that create ephemeral resources (LBs, ephemeral IPs), use tfstate reveal flags or mapping document to avoid duplicate resources.

4) Minimal infrastructure and control plane
   - Bring up networking, DNS (split-horizon if necessary), and VPNs to operator endpoints only.
   - Restore Postgres read-replica from latest snapshot. If snapshot older than RPO, spin read-only to avoid accidental writes.
   - Restore object storage bucket to object-store-compatible endpoint; validate that model artifacts (tarballs, checkpoints) are present.

5) Service-level sequencing
   - Start metadata and model registry services in read-only mode. Confirm artifact checksums.
   - Start inference runtime in limited-mode (no writeback to metadata; KV cache cold but acceptable).
   - Start routing/proxy layer with strict rate limits and canary percentage (e.g., 5%).

6) Data systems and write paths (after smoke passes)
   - Promote Postgres replica to primary according to plan if WAL replay is complete and validated.
   - Reconnect job queues and background sync workers one-at-a-time; monitor processing lag.

Verification and smoke tests (quick pass/fail checks)
- Health endpoints: /health, /live on control plane and inference pods.
- Minimal inference call: 3 short prompts across top-3 models, confirm obs tokens and latency within baseline.
- Registry checksum test: curl model storage -> sha256sum compare to stored manifest.
- DB sanity: select count(*) from key tables (should be non-zero and within expected ranges).
- KV cache priming: run a small batch of common prefixes and validate cache hit growth.

Metrics and dashboards to watch during restore
- Token per-second and avg latency (per model).
- Postgres replication lag, tx/sec, long-running queries.
- Object store error rates and 5xx.
- Node CPU/GPU utilization and OOM/killed pods.

Rollback / escape hatch
- Freeze ingress: set routing to maintenance page or redirect to hosted fallback (if contractual).
- Revert terraform partial applies using saved diff or targeted destroy for known modules.
- If primary DB promotion caused divergence, failover back to snapshot-derived read-only instance and re-evaluate WAL strategy.

Post-restore reconciliation tasks (next 24–72 hours)
- Rehydrate metrics history and tracing (ensure no sampling gaps).
- Run full consistency suite (longer checks): cross-check counts between metadata DB and object-store manifests.
- Evaluate partial writes: re-run idempotent jobs for any entries created during degraded mode.
- Schedule a staged backup: take fresh snapshots and seal them to the offsite vault.

Terraform module design notes for DR friendliness
- Each module should export a small set of stable resource IDs in outputs (cluster_id, lb_dns, db_instance_id) — makes imports simpler.
- Avoid dynamic resource names that rely on timestamps when possible. Use stable name prefixes + random suffix stored in tfstate outputs.
- Add a lightweight module, dr-import-hints, that contains guidance outputs for operator commands after snapshot restore (e.g., terraform import commands).
- Provide a "read-only" flag in deploy module configs: this switches services to safe configs on startup (no background jobs, strict rate limiting).

Model artifact and weights management
- Maintain two-tier artifact retention: current working set (hot), and DR archives (cold). Cold should be immutable and retained for at least 90 days by default.
- Verify compatible quantization/format markers in manifests — model serving will bail on mismatched formats.

Runbook examples and quick commands (annotated)
- Lock state: terraform state pull > state.json && aws s3 cp --encrypt state.json s3://dr-operators/backups/state-$(date +%s).json
- Targeted apply: terraform apply -target=module.vpc -target=module.eks -auto-approve
- Import db: terraform import module.rds.aws_db_instance.primary arn:aws:rds:us-west-2:123:db:primary-db
- Snapshot verify: aws s3 ls s3://cluster-artifacts/2026-01-01/ && aws s3 cp s3://cluster-artifacts/2026-01-01/model_v2.tar.gz - | sha256sum

Known unknowns & TODOs (open questions)
- WAL replay speed vs. recovery point: measure on benchmark customers to set sane expectations. TODO: benchmark WAL replay for Postgres with 20GB/day write rate. (owner: Luis)
- Import complexity on TF v1.6: test import flow on staging with partially damaged tfstate. (owner: Ravi)
- Edge-case: when object-store list APIs are rate-limited during restore causing long delays — need a pagination/backoff helper in restore script.

Post-incident writeup template (what to capture)
- Timeline of actions and decisions.
- Which snapshot sets were used (IDs + timestamps).
- Terraform actions (targets, imports, provider versions).
- Smoke test outputs and telemetry graphs.
- Follow-up todos and owners.

Quick reference: escalation contacts
- Oncall infra: @infra-oncall (pager: +1-555-0088)
- Eng-private-deployments lead: Maya Chen
- Customer success pager: cs-ops

End notes
This document is intentionally prescriptive but conservative — the idea is to get a safe, observable surface up quickly and then iterate to full fidelity. Keep this file as a living runbook: after each DR exercise, append the TL;DR timeline and any terraform import snippets that were necessary.

Appendix: small checklist for tabletop rehearsal (30–90 min)
- Preseed a lost-state scenario in staging and practice targeted terraform import + apply.
- Validate smoke tests (inference call + manifest checksum) within 20 minutes.
- Confirm the read-only mode prevents background reprocessing.
- Review postmortem and update this doc within 48 hours.
